title: EmberTech POC: workload mix, benchmark KPIs & timeline
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet (QPS/concurrency/token mix) by 2025-08-01
EmberTech to provide sample production traffic trace (pseudonymized) by 2025-08-04
Schedule 2-hour baseline benchmark run (remote) w/ EmberTech infra team for week of 2025-08-11
SE to send draft POC runbook and connectivity checklist by 2025-07-31
action_items: Aisha Patel; Send pricing band estimates + reserved capacity options; due 2025-08-01
Connor Lee; Prepare benchmark config (models, sequence lengths, batching params); due 2025-07-31
Priya Menon; Share 72-hour traffic sample (anonymized) and example payloads; due 2025-08-04
Diego Ramos; Confirm VPC peering window and provide contact for infra access; due 2025-08-06
header: Date: 2025-07-30 · Duration: 52 min · Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Diego, Priya, Sara (EmberTech)
summary: POC scoping call focused on workload characterization for EmberTech's conversational assistant. Primary goals: agree on QPS/concurrency targets, token distribution for benchmark, success criteria (latency/cost/quality), and POC timeline and access requirements.
topics: Current production profile and pain points
Token distribution (input vs output) and prompt variations
Benchmark plan: synthetic vs replay; duration; metrics to capture
Connectivity & security: VPC, SSO, audit logs
Success criteria and go/no-go decision points
Timeline and next steps for POC
transcript: [00:00] Aisha: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. we wanted to run through the POC scoping for the EmberTech assistant workload, make sure we're aligned on qps and what you care about for success.

[00:18] Diego: Yep thanks Aisha. we're looking to see if we can move from our in-house endpoints to a managed inference path — big ones are tail latency, cost at scale, and of course data residency — our stack is multi-region in us-west and eu-west.

[00:32] Connor: quick intro, i'm Connor on the SE side. i'll propose the benchmark plan and the traffic model we'll run. apologies if i mumbles on some names — fireflies is sometimes a little rough — but we'll share configs after the call.

[00:48] Priya: quick context — production is ~70 qps on average during peak, bursts to 260 for short windows, about 40 concurrent sessions, ops team wants 95th < 300ms for simple prompts and 99th < 1s for long gen. tokens: input averages ~50 tokens, output around 220 but with a long tail up to 1k for some summaries.
[01:12] Sara: also worth noting we run a heavy system prompt per request of ~400 tokens, that's included in the input size — reduces effective user token share but matters for compute cost.

[01:30] Connor: ok that helps. i'd like to break the workload into 3 shapes for the POC: short-turn Q&A (input 20-80, output 20-80), long summarization (input 400-1k, output 600-1k), and chat sessions which have many small turns w/ context — for modelling we'll use weights 60% short, 25% chat-turn, 15% long-summaries unless you want to tweak.

[01:58] Diego: 60/25/15 seems reasonable as a starting point. for concurrency we're seeing steady 30-50 on worker nodes but endpoints themselves show spikes when batch jobs start — we care about how redwood handles batching and prefilling kv cache.

[02:18] Connor: yes, we'll test with both batching enabled and an aggressive no-batching low-latency path. our runtime supports automatic prefix caching (KV cache) but we'll need synthetic traces to warm the cache. question: can you share a day of traffic so we can extract real session lengths and turn ratios?
[02:38] Priya: sure we can, but need to anonymize tokens. we'll export payload sizes and timestamps — not message content. i'll put that on the action items list. any preference csv/json?
[02:50] Aisha: csv with columns (timestamp, session_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, route) is perfect — it lets us run a replay and also compute token mix quickly.
[03:06] Sara: on security we need to validate SOC2 controls, SAML SSO for the console, and KMS integration for key management — also audit logs are mandatory for our compliance team.

[03:20] Connor: all standard; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit exports, and for hosted we can enable SAML and long-term retention for logs as an add-on. we'll include a security checklist in the runbook.
[03:36] Diego: awesome. now benchmarks — we want to see both latency percentiles and token cost per 1M tokens. what durations do you recommend for representative runs?

[03:48] Connor: good question. we recommend three phases: short sanity runs (30-60min) to validate configs, a 4-hour steady run to capture distributions, and a 48-hour replay to capture burst patterns and caching behavior. for the POC we'll aim for the 4-hour steady + 48-hour replay if you can allocate infra time.
[04:12] Priya: 48-hour might be tough but we can do a 24-hour replay for the first pass. we just want to catch daily traffic spikes and scheduled background jobs that skew burst profiles.

[04:24] Connor: that's fine — 24-hour is a good compromise. we'll still instrument telemetry for 99/95/50 pctiles, p50/p95/p99 latency for token generation, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and batch sizes. we'll also capture cold-start behavior for model variants.
[04:44] Aisha: quick commercial note — are you leaning towards dedicated capacity or hosted for the POC? that affects how we size and cost the run.
[04:54] Diego: initially hosted to validate performance, but if numbers look right we may move to dedicated for production. we care about cost per 1M tokens in both modes.
[05:04] Sara: and for the POC we need an estimate of what a production committed baseline would look like — we have budget windows in september.
[05:12] Aisha: we'll slot initial pricing bands in the doc; Connor will give sizing guidance based on the traffic you share. do you have preferred models?

[05:20] Priya: currently testing open models and a few tuned variants; for the benchmark we'd like to run 2-3 model variants: a cost-optimized quantized model, a medium-sized baseline, and a high-quality model for comparison.

[05:34] Connor: great — we'll include a quantized benchmark (e.g., 4-bit variant), a standard fp16 baseline, and a high-capacity variant. note: quantization can change latency profiles — we'll report quality delta as part of success criteria.

[05:48] Diego: on success criteria: ops wants stable 95th < 350ms for short-turns, p99 < 1.2s; product wants tolerable quality delta < 3% for the quantized model on our eval set; finance wants cost per 1M tokens < $X (we'll fill exact target after pricing).

[06:10] Priya: to add nuance — some of our longest gen summaries can take longer, but those are allowed higher latency as long as throughput remains. also we rely on prefix caching to reduce cost on chat sessions — cold-start penalties should be documented.

[06:28] Connor: noted. we'll capture warm vs cold metrics separately and report cache hit rates, average batch size, and per-request token counts. also we'll measure effective tokens/sec per GPU and map that to cost.
[06:42] Sara: network egress costs across regions are a factor for us, too. will your hosted numbers include cloud egress estimates or should we model that separately?
[06:52] Aisha: we'll include egress assumptions in the pricing spreadsheet, but exact cloud egress varies by region — we'll call out assumptions and let you replace with your numbers.
[07:03] Diego: can you walk through the benchmark inputs you need? Connor mentioned CSV with timestamps — anything else?

[07:10] Connor: yes — sample payloads showing system prompt length, typical user prompt, example attachments if any (we'll dummy them), and a mapping of routes to SLAs (e.g., /summarize = lower concurrency higher tokens). also SSH or VPC peering window for the remote runner if we need to run within your VPC.

[07:28] Priya: we can open a peering window for the week of 8/11 but will need IP allowlist and an account for audit logs. also we require a non-prod SLA that only our infra team uses for the benchmark window.

[07:38] Connor: understood — we'll prepare a connectivity checklist: IP ranges, firewall rules, TLS certs if needed, and a list of ports and endpoints. we'll also provide an agentless replay harness if peering is not approved.

[07:50] Aisha: timeline recap: Redwood to send runbook + pricing by 7/31; EmberTech to send traffic sample by 8/4; agree on benchmark week (target 8/11) and run 4-hour steady + 24-hour replay; follow-up demo of results within 3 business days of run completion.
[08:10] Diego: sounds good. one more technical: how do you simulate multi-turn context for chat? we need to ensure the KV cache behavior matches our session stickiness.

[08:18] Connor: for chat we'll replay sessions preserving session_id and order, so the runtime can warm KV cache. we'll instrument cache hit ratio and effective latency per turn. if you use context truncation rules we'll mimic those too.
[08:32] Priya: do you have a recommended batch size ceiling for low-latency path? we're worried about batching hiding tail latency during spikes.

[08:40] Connor: we'll test a low-latency config with batch max=1 and a throughput config with dynamic batching set to 32 or 64 depending on observed sequence lengths. we'll surface p99 differences between configs.
[08:55] Sara: any blocking compliance questions? we still need SOC2 attestation for hosted, but for the POC the compliance team will accept a security questionnaire and draft contract language.
[09:06] Aisha: we'll send the SOC2 summary and the standard security questionnaire. for contract/legal we'll attach a template MSA — we won't push for signature until you validate benchmarks.
[09:18] Diego: ok. last thing — who owns the success decision? product + infra joint sign-off; product signs on quality metrics and infra signs on latency/ops metrics.
[09:28] Aisha: perfect. we'll build the runbook with clear go/no-go thresholds and a short checklist for sign-off by product and infra.

[09:36] Connor: technical note — when we report quality delta we'll run your eval set inside the POC and compute rouge/accuracy depending on task; for chat we'll sample a human review bucket of 500 responses for qualitative assessment.
[09:52] Priya: that works. we'll prepare an evaluation set and share labeling guidance. also curious about model fallbacks — what happens if capacity is constrained mid-run?

[10:02] Connor: routing policy can fallback to a smaller model or a scoped high-availability path; for POC we'll keep everything colocated but we can test fallbacks in a separate run if you want to validate graceful degradation.
[10:16] Diego: maybe include one controlled fallback scenario in the 4-hour run — spike a synthetic load and verify latency degradation and model fallback behavior.
[10:26] Aisha: noted. i'll add that as an optional test in the runbook. any other questions?
[10:32] Priya: timeline and next steps look clear. just want to confirm the data we share is only payload sizes and timestamps, not message text. we'll anonymize before sending.
[10:42] Connor: perfect. one more minor ask — if you have a list of top 20 user intents we can map to model routes, that will help tune batching and caching heuristics.
[10:52] Diego: yes, we'll include that. thanks everyone.
[10:56] Aisha: thanks folks. i'll follow up with the doc and pricing. recap of action items and we'll sync early next week if any blockers pop up. bye!
